entries.name: 12pc Wedgie Bread
entries.serving: 1 order of 12 garlic cheese bread wedges
entries.src: estimated: no published Pizza 73 nutrition found, comparable to a generic garlic cheese bread wedge order scaled to 12 pieces
entries.note: He got this one as a BOGO promo item alongside a burger order; treat it as a side to split, not a full serving. A few wedges rather than the whole 12 keeps the carbs in check.

entries.name: 4Pc Signature Chicken Combo, Spicy, Leg & Thigh, Cajun Fries, Iced Tea
entries.serving: 1 combo: 4 pc spicy dark-meat chicken, regular Cajun fries, biscuit, bottled Fuze iced tea
entries.src: derived from Popeyes Canada published 4-piece chicken nutrition (approx. 830 kcal for dark meat), published biscuit and Cajun fries figures, sweetened iced tea estimated
entries.note: The single heaviest item in this file: 1,560 kcal is nearly a full day's calorie target in one order. Swapping the iced tea for a diet drink and fries for mashed potatoes (see the other combo variant below) cuts close to 300 kcal for the same chicken and protein.

entries.name: 4Pc Signature Chicken Combo, Spicy, Mixed, Mashed Potatoes, Diet Coke
entries.serving: 1 combo: 4 pc spicy mixed dark and white meat chicken, mashed potatoes with Cajun gravy, biscuit, bottled Diet Coke
entries.src: derived from Popeyes Canada published 4-piece chicken nutrition, published mashed potatoes and biscuit figures, Diet Coke is 0 kcal
entries.note: This is the combo variant he should default to over the fries-and-sweet-tea version above: same chicken and protein, roughly 290 fewer kcal, just from the side and drink choice.

entries.name: Banana Chocolate Chunk Muffin
entries.src: McDonald's Canada published nutrition (430 kcal, as shown on his DoorDash order screen); carbs/fat split corrected to 73C/13F to match McDonald's own published breakdown, the old 65C/15F split didn't match
entries.note: Almost pure carbs and fat with very little protein; on retatrutide with an underrating risk, this is fine as extra calories but shouldn't replace a protein-bearing item in the same order.

entries.name: BBQ Loaded Pizza Slice (Large)
entries.serving: 1 of 8 slices, BBQ sauce, pepperoni, beef, spicy BBQ chicken, garlic, chilli flakes, cilantro (no sausage)
entries.src: estimated: no published Calgary Pizza Master nutrition found, comparable to a generic loaded meat BBQ pizza slice; modeled with beef pepperoni in place of pork pepperoni (confirm with the shop); sausage topping dropped from the build and its calories/macros subtracted, see note
entries.note: The shop's sausage topping is pork by default and has no confirmed non-pork version, so it was excluded from this build entirely rather than guessed at. Otherwise similar profile to the butter chicken build, slightly leaner because BBQ sauce carries less fat than the creamy butter chicken base.

entries.name: Beefy Bacon Cheddar Cheese Burger
entries.serving: 1 burger, white bun, lettuce, tomato, red onion, Flipp'n sauce, mayo, garlic, cheddar, bacon
entries.src: estimated: no published Flipp'n Burgers nutrition found, comparable to a generic bacon cheddar smash-style burger; modeled with beef bacon in place of pork bacon since he doesn't eat pork (confirm with the shop which bacon they use)
entries.note: Two sauces (Flipp'n sauce and mayo) on one burger; dropping one is a simple 80 to 100 kcal trim.

entries.name: Big Boy Smash Burger Combo
entries.serving: 1 combo: three smash patties, melted cheese, lettuce, tomato, smash sauce, side fries, Diet Pepsi
entries.src: estimated: no published PrimeTime Donair & Poutine nutrition found, comparable to a triple smash-patty burger combo with fries
entries.note: High protein from three patties, but fat is also very high, over the full 60 g daily fat target in one meal. Two patties instead of three would keep this a high-protein order while cutting roughly 250 kcal and 20 g fat.

entries.name: Black Coffee
entries.src: USDA FDC 173806, brewed coffee
entries.note: Can blunt appetite further, watch total intake if already skipping meals.

entries.name: Butter Chicken Bowl
entries.src: estimated: no published Foodyard nutrition found, comparable to a standard butter chicken and rice bowl
entries.note: A reasonably balanced bowl order; the butter chicken cream sauce is the fat source, everything else is lean.

entries.name: Butter Chicken Loaded Pizza Slice (Large)
entries.serving: 1 of 8 slices, butter chicken sauce, salami, bacon, tandoori chicken, garlic, chilli flakes, cilantro (no sausage)
entries.src: estimated: no published Calgary Pizza Master nutrition found, comparable to a generic loaded meat pizza slice with a creamy sauce; modeled with beef salami and turkey bacon in place of the usual pork versions since he doesn't eat pork (confirm with the shop); sausage topping dropped from the build and its calories/macros subtracted, see note
entries.note: The shop's sausage topping is pork by default and has no confirmed non-pork version, unlike the salami and bacon here, so it was excluded from this build entirely rather than guessed at. Three meat toppings plus a rich butter chicken sauce remains: two slices of this is still a meaningful chunk of the daily fat target.

entries.name: Cheese Dog (his build)
entries.serving: 1 all-beef hot dog with cheese, mayo, ketchup, A.1. sauce, BBQ sauce, tomatoes, jalapenos, grilled mushrooms, grilled onions
entries.src: derived: Five Guys published Cheese Dog base (fastfoodnutrition.org, 615 kcal/41F/41C/22P) plus published per-topping figures for all four sauces he adds (mayo 100 kcal/11F, ketchup 15 kcal/4C, BBQ sauce 60 kcal/16C, A.1. sauce approx. 15 kcal/3C per Kraft's label), free veggie toppings treated as negligible; a plain cheese dog cannot be lower than this build, so the prior 530 kcal figure was wrong
entries.note: Four full-strength sauces (mayo, ketchup, A.1., BBQ) on one hot dog add roughly 200 kcal and 11 g fat over the plain cheese dog; picking one or two sauces instead of all four is the easy trim here, not the 10 to 15 g this file used to claim.

entries.name: Cheeseburger (his build)
entries.serving: 1 cheeseburger (two beef patties, standard Five Guys default), mayo, ketchup, BBQ sauce, tomatoes, jalapenos, green peppers, grilled mushrooms, grilled onions
entries.src: derived: Five Guys published Cheeseburger base (two patties, 840 kcal/47P/40C/55F) plus published per-topping figures for the three sauces he adds (mayo 100 kcal/11F, ketchup 15 kcal/4C, BBQ sauce 60 kcal/16C); a single mayo packet alone is 90 to 100 kcal, so the old +40 kcal estimate for three sauces was too low
entries.note: Five Guys' regular cheeseburger is two patties by default; a Little Cheeseburger (one patty) would roughly halve the base while keeping most of the toppings he actually likes (mushrooms, grilled onions, peppers). Mayo alone is close to 100 kcal of the sauce total here, dropping it is the biggest single trim.

entries.name: Chicken Alfredo Pasta
entries.src: Domino's Canada published nutrition, Chicken Alfredo Pasta (regular)
entries.note: He orders 2 at a time. Alfredo sauce is the fat driver here (17 g of the 28 g is saturated per Domino's own numbers); a marinara-based pasta would keep the protein and cut 10-plus grams of fat.

entries.name: Chicken Biriyani Combo
entries.serving: 1 combo platter with rice, chicken biryani, side salad/raita, plus a Diet Cola
entries.src: estimated: no published Biryani Garden nutrition found, comparable to a typical South Asian chicken biryani combo platter portion
entries.note: Rice-heavy dish that alone covers most of his daily 165 g carb target. Eating half the rice and keeping all the chicken would shift this toward a much better protein-to-carb ratio for his goals.

entries.name: Chicken McMuffin
entries.serving: 1 muffin sandwich, chicken patty, cheese, mayo-style sauce, butter
entries.src: McDonald's Canada published nutrition (360 kcal, as shown per-component on his DoorDash order screen)
entries.note: He orders 2 at a time. Decent breakfast protein source relative to its size.

entries.name: Chicken Shawarma Platter #7
entries.serving: 1 platter, chicken shawarma, garlic sauce, spicy garlic, sweet sauce, Greek salad
entries.src: estimated: no published Shawarma Palace nutrition found, comparable to a typical chicken shawarma platter with rice/salad and multiple sauces
entries.note: Three sauces on one platter (garlic, spicy garlic, sweet donair sauce) stack up fat fast. Picking one sauce instead of all three is a realistic 100-plus kcal save.

entries.name: Chipotle Beef Bacon Fries
entries.serving: 1 order, loaded fries with beef bacon and chipotle sauce
entries.src: estimated: no published Boardwalk Fries Burgers Shakes nutrition found, comparable to a generic loaded bacon fries side
entries.note: Already uses beef bacon, so no pork substitution needed here. He orders 2 of these alongside the burger combos above; loaded fries plus a burger combo in one order is a very large total, worth splitting across two sittings.

entries.name: Chipotle Burger Combo (Single, Regular Bun, Tater Bites, Diet Cola)
entries.serving: 1 combo, single chipotle burger, regular bun, small tater bites, fountain diet cola
entries.src: estimated: no published Boardwalk Fries Burgers Shakes nutrition found, comparable to a standard smash burger combo with a small fried side
entries.note: Diet cola instead of regular soda is already the right call here and saves roughly 150 kcal versus a sugared drink.

entries.name: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar
entries.serving: 1 can/serving (355 ml) from a 2 L bottle he buys at Shell
entries.src: Coca-Cola published nutrition, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar is 0 kcal per serving
entries.note: Zero calorie, no macro impact. Fine to log purely for hydration/habit tracking.

entries.name: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, 330 mL can
entries.src: Coca-Cola Canada nutrition page 2025

entries.name: Coca-Cola Zero Sugar, 500 mL
entries.src: Coca-Cola Canada nutrition page 2025, scaled from per 100 mL value of 0 kcal
entries.note: His usual pour from the 2 L bottle he orders.

entries.name: Creatine Monohydrate
entries.src: USDA FDC, creatine monohydrate is metabolically inert, 0 kcal per serving
entries.note: Timing does not matter, only daily consistency does. Take with water any time of day.

entries.name: Crispy Cilantro Lime Loaded Bowl w/ Cheese
entries.src: estimated from comparable Tim Hortons loaded bowl items; Tim Hortons does publish Canadian nutrition for this line but the exact figure for this specific bowl was not confirmed here, so treat as an estimate until checked against timhortons.ca
entries.note: Worth checking Tim Hortons' own nutrition page for the exact number since they do publish it; this is a placeholder estimate in the meantime.

entries.name: Dave's Single
entries.serving: 1 burger, quarter pound beef, cheese, mayo, ketchup, lettuce, tomato, onion, bun (premium or regular)
entries.src: Wendy's Canada published nutrition, Dave's Single (590 kcal, as also shown on his DoorDash order screen)
entries.note: He has ordered it with the premium bun and with the plain sandwich bun; the difference is small, roughly 20 kcal. Dropping mayo would save about 90 kcal and 10 g fat for minimal taste loss on a burger this simple.

entries.name: Fuze Iced Tea
entries.src: Fuze Beverage Canada nutrition label

entries.name: Go Bucket, 1 Drumstick + Individual Fries
entries.serving: 1 Original Recipe drumstick plus individual fries
entries.src: derived: KFC Canada's own current nutrition sheet (kfc.ca, updated Feb 18 2025) lists Original Recipe Drumstick at 140 kcal/8F/2C/15P, unchanged from the earlier note here, plus Seasoned French Fries Individual size at 310 kcal/13F/45C/5P. Summed that is 450 kcal, not the 370 kcal this entry used to show; the drumstick figure was already right, the fries portion was undercounted
entries.note: Best protein-per-calorie chicken item in his whole KFC rotation, but the individual fries side is most of this combo's calories (310 of 450). He orders multiples of these Go Buckets in a single order; more drumsticks and fewer fries/wraps would push his overall protein up for a similar calorie total.

entries.name: Go Bucket, 1 Original Recipe Tender + Individual Fries
entries.serving: 1 Original Recipe tender plus individual fries, no KFC sauce
entries.src: derived from KFC Canada published Original Recipe tender and individual fries nutrition
entries.note: He skips the KFC sauce on this one already, which is the right move; keep doing that.

entries.name: Go Bucket, Regular Snacker Wrap + Individual Fries
entries.serving: 1 regular Snacker Wrap plus individual fries
entries.src: derived from KFC Canada published Snacker Wrap and individual fries nutrition
entries.note: Low protein for the calorie count. Two of these plus a piece of Original Recipe chicken would hit more protein for similar total kcal.

entries.name: Go Bucket, Spicy Snacker Wrap + Individual Fries
entries.serving: 1 spicy Snacker Wrap plus individual fries
entries.src: derived from KFC Canada published Snacker Wrap and individual fries nutrition, spicy sauce estimated similar to regular
entries.note: Same profile as the regular Snacker Wrap; spice adds negligible calories.

entries.name: Half & Half (Large, Chicken Shawarma, Garlic Sauce)
entries.serving: 1 large Half & Half bowl, chicken shawarma, medium garlic sauce, lettuce, tomatoes/hot peppers vary by order
entries.src: estimated: no published Osmow's Canada nutrition found, comparable to a large mixed rice-and-fries shawarma bowl with garlic sauce
entries.note: He has ordered this with garlic sauce mixed in and also with garlic sauce on the side; on the side lets him control the amount, worth using every time to cut 50 to 100 kcal of sauce.

entries.name: Hot Honey Chicken (6 inch, Ghostpepper Bread)
entries.serving: 1 six inch sub, Ghostpepper Bread, toasted, habanero jack, hot honey sauce, mayonnaise, garlic aioli
entries.src: derived from Subway Canada published bread, chicken, cheese and sauce component nutrition
entries.note: Mayonnaise plus garlic aioli together are close to 170 kcal and 19 g fat of the total. Dropping one of the two sauces keeps the sub recognizable and saves close to that amount.

entries.name: Hot Honey Chipotle Grilled Chicken (6 inch, his build)
entries.serving: 1 six inch sub, toasted, Italian Herbs & Cheese or Flatbread, habanero jack, hot honey sauce, chipotle southwest (sometimes mayo and garlic aioli added)
entries.src: derived from Subway Canada published bread, grilled chicken, cheese and sauce nutrition components, summed
entries.note: He orders this two ways: one with hot honey plus chipotle southwest, one with hot honey plus mayo and garlic aioli. Both are two full-fat sauce packets. Dropping to one sauce (hot honey alone) saves roughly 100 to 130 kcal and 15 to 20 g fat without losing the sub.

entries.name: Large Cajun Fries
entries.serving: 1 large order (Five Guys portions are notoriously oversized, roughly double a typical large fries elsewhere)
entries.src: Five Guys published nutrition for Large Cajun Style Fries (myfooddiary.com/fatsecret aggregation of Five Guys' own figures): 1328 kcal, 57 g fat, 184 g carbs, 20 g protein; the previous split (71F/154C/18P) had the fat and carbs numbers swapped-ish and didn't match the published breakdown
entries.note: This one order of fries is close to his entire daily carb target by itself. Splitting a large order across two meals, or ordering Regular instead of Large, is the single biggest easy save in his whole order history.

entries.name: Mango Juice
entries.src: estimated, comparable to a standard restaurant mango juice/nectar serving, no published figure found
entries.note: 44 g of straight sugar-equivalent carbs with zero protein. Water or a diet drink alongside the platter would free up real carb budget for the meal itself.

entries.name: Milk, 2%
entries.src: USDA FDC 746782, 2% milk
entries.note: Cheapest protein-per-effort drink he has, worth defaulting to over water when appetite is low.

entries.name: Mix Chicken, Lamb & Beef Shawarma Platter #11 (no donair)
entries.serving: 1 platter, mixed chicken/lamb/beef shawarma, garlic sauce, spicy garlic, sweet sauce, Greek salad
entries.src: estimated: no published Shawarma Palace nutrition found, comparable to a mixed lamb/beef/chicken shawarma platter with multiple sauces
entries.note: Same order from both the Montgomery and Carrington locations. Lamb pushes the fat noticeably above the pure chicken platter #7; if protein is the priority over flavor variety, the chicken-only platter is the better default.

entries.name: Multivitamin, one a day
entries.src: Centrum Canada product label
entries.note: Take with a meal for absorption, but do not stress the exact timing, daily consistency is what counts.

entries.name: Nashville-Style Hot Chicken (6 inch, his loaded build)
entries.serving: 1 six inch sub, Italian Herbs & Cheese toasted, 2x habanero jack, chipotle southwest, garlic aioli, peppercorn ranch
entries.src: derived from Subway Canada published bread, chicken, double-cheese and sauce component nutrition, summed for a 3-sauce build seen in his order history
entries.note: Biggest lean-swap opportunity in his whole Subway rotation. Chipotle southwest, garlic aioli and peppercorn ranch stacked together are roughly 280 kcal and 30 g fat of pure sauce. Same sandwich with just one of these saves 250 to 300 kcal, no change to bread, cheese, or protein.

entries.name: Nashville-Style Hot Chicken (6 inch, standard build)
entries.serving: 1 six inch sub, Italian Herbs & Cheese toasted, 2x habanero jack, crispy onions, Nashville-style hot sauce, garlic aioli
entries.src: derived from Subway Canada published bread, chicken, double-cheese and sauce component nutrition
entries.note: His best-balanced Subway build: 35 g protein for 610 kcal is a solid ratio for the daily 150 g protein target. Double cheese is the main add-on versus a single-cheese sub, worth roughly 50 kcal and 4 g fat.

entries.name: On The Rocks Bowl (Large, Chicken Shawarma, Garlic Sauce)
entries.serving: 1 large bowl, chicken shawarma, medium garlic sauce, lettuce, tomatoes, onions
entries.src: estimated: no published Osmow's Canada nutrition found, comparable to a large fries-or-rice shawarma bowl with a medium serving of garlic sauce (garlic sauce is a toum-style emulsion, essentially all fat)
entries.note: Garlic sauce (toum) is oil-based and is most of the fat here. Asking for 'light garlic sauce' instead of medium would plausibly cut 150 to 200 kcal and 15 to 20 g fat without changing the order otherwise.

entries.name: On The Stix (Regular, Chicken Shawarma, Garlic Sauce, Spicy)
entries.serving: 1 regular skewer-style order, chicken shawarma, garlic sauce, little spicy, tomatoes, onions, hot peppers
entries.src: estimated: no published Osmow's Canada nutrition found, comparable to a regular-size shawarma skewer platter
entries.note: Lighter than his Large orders from the same chain. Good protein-per-calorie choice when he wants Osmow's without going all the way to a Large.

entries.name: Pepperoni Pizza Slice (Large)
entries.serving: 1 of 8 slices from a large pepperoni pizza
entries.src: estimated: no published Calgary Pizza Master nutrition found, comparable to a generic large pepperoni pizza slice; modeled with beef pepperoni since standard pepperoni is pork and he doesn't eat pork (confirm with the shop which pepperoni they use)
entries.note: He and a friend split a BOGO large pizza order, so realistic serving is 2 to 4 slices, not the whole pie.

entries.name: Peri Peri Rice Platter (Regular)
entries.serving: 1 regular platter, peri peri chicken over rice
entries.src: estimated: no published Chicken World nutrition found, comparable to a typical peri peri chicken and rice platter
entries.note: He orders 4 of these at once, likely feeding more than one person; treat the per-platter numbers above as the single-serving figure.

entries.name: Shawarma Wrap (Regular, Chicken, Garlic Sauce)
entries.serving: 1 regular chicken shawarma wrap, garlic sauce, mild, lettuce, tomatoes, onions
entries.src: estimated: no published Osmow's Canada nutrition found, comparable to a standard chicken shawarma wrap with garlic sauce
entries.note: His most portable Osmow's order and a reasonable single-meal protein source.

entries.name: Side of Inferno Sauce
entries.src: estimated, comparable to a small hot sauce side, no published figure found
entries.note: Negligible calories, mostly flavor, not a lever worth touching.

entries.name: Signature Sauce (side)
entries.src: estimated, comparable to a standard fast-food mayo-based dip cup, no published Popeyes Canada figure found for this specific sauce
entries.note: Pure added fat with no protein. Easy to skip entirely without changing the meal.

entries.name: SubDog (6 inch, his build)
entries.serving: 1 six inch SubDog, habanero jack, crispy onions, hot honey sauce, mayonnaise, garlic aioli
entries.src: derived from Subway Canada published SubDog base plus bread, cheese and sauce component nutrition
entries.note: Worst protein-per-calorie sub in his rotation: three sauces (hot honey, mayonnaise, garlic aioli) add roughly 200 kcal and 23 g fat on top of the dog itself, for only 21 g protein. Cutting to just hot honey would save close to 170 kcal and 19 g fat.

entries.name: Tea with Milk
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC brewed tea (0 kcal) plus 30 mL 2% milk (~20 kcal)
entries.note: Traditional Bangladeshi style cha, a small daily protein and calorie top-up, harmless at this size.

entries.name: Teriyaki Crunch (6 inch, his loaded build)
entries.serving: 1 six inch sub, Italian Herbs & Cheese toasted, processed cheddar, crispy onions, jalapenos, plus up to 5 sauces (Nashville-style hot, mayonnaise, chipotle southwest, sweet onion teriyaki, garlic aioli)
entries.src: derived from Subway Canada published bread, chicken, cheese and sauce component nutrition, summed for a 5-sauce build seen in his order history
entries.note: His heaviest sauce-stack sub: up to five sauces on one sandwich. Trimming to just sweet onion teriyaki would save roughly 250 to 300 kcal and 30 g fat while keeping the flavor he actually orders it for.

entries.name: The Sando (Mild)
entries.src: estimated: no published Flirty Bird nutrition found, comparable to a standard Nashville hot fried chicken sandwich
entries.note: Fried chicken sandwiches like this usually carry 30 to 40 g fat mostly from the fry oil and the mayo-based sauce; asking for sauce on the side is the easy trim.

entries.name: The Tenders (Mild, Comeback Sauce)
entries.serving: 1 order of tenders, mild spice, with Comeback Sauce
entries.src: estimated: no published Flirty Bird nutrition found, comparable to a standard fried chicken tender order with a mayo-based dipping sauce
entries.note: Comeback sauce is mayo-based; ordering it on the side and using less would meaningfully cut the fat here.

entries.name: Vuna Khichuri, Beef
entries.serving: 1 order, mixed lentil-rice khichuri with bhuna-style beef
entries.src: estimated: no published Spice Avenue nutrition found, comparable to a typical Bengali beef bhuna khichuri portion
entries.note: Higher fat than the chicken version because beef bhuna carries more fat per gram of meat.

entries.name: Vuna Khichuri, Chicken
entries.serving: 1 order, mixed lentil-rice khichuri with bhuna-style chicken
entries.src: estimated: no published Spice Avenue nutrition found, comparable to a typical Bengali chicken bhuna khichuri portion
entries.note: One of the more balanced items in this file: rice, lentils and chicken together rather than a straight fried item. The bhuna gravy oil is the main fat source; asking for less oil would trim a few grams of fat without changing the dish.

entries.name: 3-Tender Combo, No/Lite spice (no fries)
entries.src: daveshotchickenmenu.us nutrition aggregator, values vary 490-550 kcal by spice level across sources. Beacon Hill NW location
entries.note: Skip the fries side and slaw comes with less fat than the mac and cheese option. Breading adds carbs, this is not a lean cut but the protein total is solid.

entries.name: Air fryer chicken breast
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC boneless skinless chicken breast raw, cooked yield adjusted

entries.name: Air fryer chicken thighs (2, seasoned)
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC boneless skinless chicken thigh raw, cooked yield adjusted, oil spray
entries.note: Season, air fry, done. No sauce.

entries.name: Almonds
entries.src: Costco Canada Kirkland Signature packaging nutrition facts

entries.name: Aloo bhaji (potato fry)
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC raw potato plus pan-fry oil ratio

entries.name: Baked salmon fillet (farmed Atlantic)
entries.src: USDA FDC, Atlantic salmon farmed cooked dry heat (206 kcal per 100 g), scaled to a 170 g cooked fillet. Previously cited raw wild Atlantic salmon, which is not commercially sold in Canada.

entries.name: Banana

entries.name: Banh Mi, Grilled Chicken (no pate)
entries.src: estimated from a standard Vietnamese banh mi with grilled chicken, pate and mayo reduced
entries.note: Ask for no pate (it is usually pork liver based) and mayo on the side. Chicken or tofu fillings only, skip any pork-based versions like banh mi thit.

entries.name: Basmati rice, raw
entries.src: USDA FDC, basmati rice raw
entries.note: Common Bangladeshi grocer and Superstore brands: Kohinoor, Tilda, Royal.

entries.name: BCAA Powder, 1 scoop
entries.src: Optimum Nutrition BCAA Canada label
entries.note: Not a real substitute for whole protein grams, useful only around training if he trains fasted.

entries.name: Beef bhuna
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC beef chuck raw, onion, oil, home-recipe ratios

entries.name: Beef Bulgogi (250g raw portion)
entries.src: Beacon Hill NW, no published nutrition, estimated from 250g marinated beef bulgogi
entries.note: This menu also sells pork belly (samgyeopsal), order beef or chicken cuts only. Do not order the pork items.

entries.name: Beef Bulgogi Bowl
entries.src: estimated similarly to the chicken bulgogi bowl, adjusted for beef's higher fat content
entries.note: Same modification as the chicken version: rice half portion, ask for extra meat instead of extra rice.

entries.name: Beef curry (jhol style)
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC beef chuck raw and standard curry gravy ratios
entries.note: More gravy than bhuna.

entries.name: Beef kala bhuna
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC beef chuck raw, long slow-cooked with heavy oil, Chittagong style
entries.note: Darker, oilier than standard bhuna.

entries.name: Beef Seekh Kabab Platter (2 kababs, rice, salad)
entries.src: kolachibbq.ca menu, no published nutrition, estimated from 2x100g grilled minced beef kabab plus 1 cup rice and salad
entries.note: Ask for rice on the side and only eat half of it, the kabab meat is the protein value here, not the rice.

entries.name: Beef stewing cubes, lean, raw
entries.src: USDA FDC, beef chuck raw, lean trim

entries.name: Black beans, canned, drained
entries.src: USDA FDC, black beans canned drained

entries.name: Blueberries, fresh
entries.src: USDA FDC, blueberries raw

entries.name: Boiled eggs (2 whole)
entries.src: USDA FDC whole egg, hard boiled

entries.name: Burrito Bowl, Double Grilled Chicken, no rice, extra lettuce and salsa
entries.src: derived from Mucho Burrito's published per-filling data (chorizo filling is 300 kcal/21P/2C/23F per mynetdiary), grilled chicken filling doubled plus vegetables, no rice, no cheese, no sour cream
entries.note: Skip rice, cheese, and sour cream entirely, use salsa and lettuce for volume instead of queso. Building it this way turns a 1000+ kcal burrito into one of the better bowls on this list.

entries.name: Butter Chicken Crispy Chicken Wrap
entries.src: foodyard.ca menu, estimated from description (fried chicken patty, butter chicken sauce, slaw in wrap); same restaurant as foodyard-butter-chicken-bowl, added separately from the menu rather than from his order history
entries.note: Ask if the chicken can be grilled instead of crispy fried. Sauce goes on the side either way, this wrap's fat is mostly the fry and the mayo-heavy sauce.

entries.name: Butter Chicken with rice
entries.src: twistoftaj.net menu, estimated from cream/butter-heavy tomato gravy plus boneless chicken thigh plus rice
entries.note: Ask for the cream sauce on the side and spoon it over lightly. This dish is the fat trap of the menu, not the protein win.

entries.name: Butter Chicken, half rice, sauce on side
entries.src: estimated from a standard Indian delivery butter chicken order with the cream sauce portion controlled and rice halved
entries.note: Spoon the cream sauce over the chicken lightly instead of pouring the whole container. Most of the fat in butter chicken is the sauce, not the meat.

entries.name: California Roll plus extra salmon sashimi side
entries.src: estimated from a standard 8-piece California roll plus 4 pieces of salmon sashimi
entries.note: If you want a roll for the texture, add a sashimi side rather than a second roll, it boosts protein without stacking more rice.

entries.name: Canned tuna in oil, drained
entries.src: Clover Leaf Canada nutrition facts, flaked light tuna in oil

entries.name: Canned tuna in water, drained
entries.src: Clover Leaf Canada nutrition facts, flaked light tuna in water

entries.name: Casein Protein Powder, 1 scoop
entries.src: Optimum Nutrition Gold Standard Casein Canada label
entries.note: Slow digesting, best last thing before bed since appetite is already gone by evening anyway.

entries.name: Chana dal (split chickpea dal)
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC cooked chana dal plus tempering oil

entries.name: Cheddar cheese, block
entries.src: Balderson Canada nutrition facts, old cheddar

entries.name: Chicken and rice meal prep bowl
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC chicken breast cooked, white rice cooked, and steamed vegetables

entries.name: Chicken Basil Stir-fry (Pad Krapow, no rice)
entries.src: estimated from a standard Thai basil chicken stir-fry, rice ordered separately or skipped
entries.note: Order the rice as a separate small side or skip it, this is a much better protein-to-calorie dish than pad Thai at the same restaurant.

entries.name: Chicken bhuna (dry curry)
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC chicken thigh raw, onion, oil, reduced-gravy method
entries.note: Less gravy than jhol, more oil per gram.

entries.name: Chicken biryani
entries.src: derived from USDA FDC basmati rice raw, chicken thigh raw, ghee, standard biryani ratios
entries.note: Rice is part of this dish, not logged separately.

entries.name: Chicken Biryani
entries.src: twistoftaj.net menu, estimated from typical dum-style chicken biryani portion (150g chicken, 2.5 cups rice, oil/ghee)

entries.name: Protein Bar
entries.src: Quest Nutrition Canada nutrition label: 200 kcal, 21 g protein, 8 g fat are printed as-is; the label's Total Carbohydrate line reads about 21 to 22 g, but roughly 14 to 17 g of that is fibre plus a small amount of sugar alcohol, neither of which Quest counts at 4 kcal/g. The carbs field here stores the net-carb figure (about 6 g) rather than total carbohydrate, so the logged macros reconcile with the printed 200 kcal instead of overshooting it
entries.note: Good backup protein hit for a low appetite day, easier to get down than a shake or a meal late in the day. Quest's 200 kcal is a net-carb calorie count, fibre and sugar alcohols are subtracted before the math, which is why the printed total carbohydrate (about 21 g) looks like it should add up to more than 200 kcal. That is a legitimate labeling convention, not a data error, so the carbs value logged here is net carbs, not total carbs.
